Subject: Prefetch behavior and roadmap alignment for Acme Health POC

Simon / Sarah — thanks again for the call this morning. Two quick follow-ups from our side to make sure the POC hit next week is scoped correctly: 

1) Clarify prefetch intent: you mentioned CloudCove will warm prompt prefixes for the clinical summarization flow and that some requests will require low-latency cold starts. Can you confirm what fraction of requests you expect to be cold vs warmed (ballpark %)?

2) SLA ask: Acme asked whether we can guarantee 200ms p50 on warmed sessions and an SLO exception for cold starts during the first 72 hours of rollout while they ramp traffic. We need to decide whether this is a sales exception or technical change.

Internal note / ask to the eng leads: Marissa / Logan / Tessa — please advise on the feasibility of the SLA exception and any short-term runtime mitigations we should propose (e.g., temporary dedicated warm pool, prefix-only caching, or a graceful fallback model). I attached a one-page playbook draft with suggested mitigations.

Simon — attaching our playbook draft and a suggested timeline. If you can provide the cold vs warm split (even rough), we can finalize a small-scope plan.

Attachments: Acme-prefetch-playbook-v1.docx

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly — quick answers from our side: 

- Cold vs warmed: on day 0 we expect ~60% cold, 40% warmed as users access new patient threads. Over the first 48–72 hours of traffic shaping we expect warmed to increase to ~75% as CloudCove primes common prefixes and sequences.
- SLA expectation: their engineering lead is comfortable with a p50 200ms on warmed paths, but they want an escalation path if cold starts exceed 1s at p95. The main risk is initial ramp when several workflows touch new patient documents concurrently.

We can commit to sharing traffic heatmaps during the POC. For next steps: a short call with runtime to validate warm-pool sizing would be helpful — Sarah, can you coordinate a slot?

Simon
Simon Park

Short technical note / action items from runtime: 

- Feasibility: We can meet the warmed p50 200ms target with a small dedicated warm pool and aggressive prefix/KV caching. For the initial burst (60% cold) we expect p95 cold starts around 800ms–1.2s on our standard quantized model on A100-sized nodes. That aligns with Acme's tolerance but we should be explicit about the p95 cold windows.
- Fast mitigations (POC): 
  * Provision a 3-node warm pool (estimated 4 GPU-hours/day during the POC) — quick to spin up via Dedicated.
  * Enable prefix-only prefetching for the summarization flow (reduces cold p95 by ~30–40%).
  * Add an early-fallback to a smaller, lower-latency model for requests hitting >1s (configurable by route).

- Operational runbook items for the 72-hour grace window: 
  1) On p95 cold >1s trigger: page oncall-runtime and Sales Eng lead (Marissa).
  2) Runtime to temporarily increase warm pool until traffic stabilizes.
  3) Share heatmaps daily with Acme and CloudCove; roll off warm pool when warmed% >70% for 24 hours.

I'll prepare a short ops estimate and send by end of day Thursday — Marissa, ballpark pricing for temporary capacity will help finalize the SOW.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Sr. Manager, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference
